beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Hey — good news, I actually joined the tour."

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "But it's brought up a lot. Can you do a full reading this time — past, present, future?"

options.text: There was a real choice behind you — two paths, and neither one was wrong to want.
It means you made the wrong choice back then.
This card just means you should've stayed with the band.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "I turned down staying with my old band to do this. I still think about that sometimes."

options.text: That's worth sitting with, not dismissing — a real choice means weighing every angle, even after.
Then you should regret it.
Once a choice is made, it doesn't matter anymore.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Sometimes I still feel like two different people — the one in the old band and the one on this tour."

options.text: Both are still you — this card's about holding both sides of yourself in balance, not picking one to erase.
It means you should let go of the old version of yourself completely.
It means one of those two sides just needs to be nurtured until it takes over.
Right now, something in you is genuinely flourishing — real growth, not forced.
It means you're being lazy about your career.
Growth isn't really what this card is about.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "I've been writing so much more since I joined. It doesn't even feel like work."

options.text: That ease is the point — pleasure and creativity aren't indulgences, they're the message.
Enjoying it that much probably means you're not taking it seriously.
How it feels doesn't matter, only the output does.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Do you think something is actually coming out of all this writing?"

options.text: Something's ready to be born — an idea or a project finally taking real shape.
It means you're standing at the edge of something totally unrelated to the writing.
It means you'll have to choose between the writing and the tour.
Another fresh start is coming — one thing wrapping up right as the next one opens.
It means this is all about to fall apart.
The future isn't really what this card addresses.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "The tour ends in a few months. I don't know what happens after that."

options.text: You don't need to know yet — trust the path shows up once you take the next step.
You should be panicking about that, honestly.
Not knowing means you should stop and turn back now.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Do I need to make peace with turning down my old band?"

options.text: Less about peace, more about trusting you chose with your gut, not just the safer plan.
No, you should still regret it.
That choice doesn't need any more thought.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Is it okay that I'm not stressed about any of this right now?"

options.text: More than okay — it's a reminder to care for yourself first, not treat calm as a warning sign.
You should be more stressed than you are.
Stress levels don't factor into a reading.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "What if I just end up starting over from nothing again?"

options.text: Starting over isn't the risk — it's a beginner's mind, curious instead of already jaded.
Then you'll have wasted this whole tour for nothing.
Starting over doesn't mean anything in this context.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Some of my old bandmates think I made a reckless choice, going off script like this."

options.text: That's the nonconformist energy of this card — willing to go against convention, not reckless for its own sake.
It means you need to weigh their opinion carefully before deciding anything else.
It means you should protect yourself from their opinions the way you'd protect something still growing.

beats.speaker: reader
beats.text: One more thing — the Fool travels light too. Whatever's next, you don't have to carry everything from before into it.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Thanks. That's exactly what I needed to hear."
